title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 7
text: Since it was time, I hopped into Chick’s carriage—which she’d pulled over as if nothing were amiss—along with Raphtalia, and we set off. We’re planning a bit of a long trip.

We’re going to hold serious negotiations with our chocolate supplier. Of course, the supplier is a chocolate farmer. I can’t help but wonder over and over again, “What kind of farmer is that, anyway?”

Right now, we’re sourcing the chocolate in the village from a farmer introduced to us by a business contact, but there’s another farmer who seems willing to sell it a bit cheaper, so we’re heading there. Our challenge is to secure high-quality chocolate at the lowest possible price.

The reason is that this chocolate farmer is apparently the family home of the Robin Hood-like figure. So, maybe they’ll sell it to us at a discount thanks to family connections… or something like that. However, when I recall our conversation from back then, he said something that still bugs me a little. If I remember correctly…
“Shield Hero, come to think of it, what are you doing for Valentine’s Day?”
“Valentine’s Day? Come to think of it, the merchants were talking about that. Does that exist in this world, too?”
“Yes. My family runs a chocolate farm, and since they’ve been helping us out in various ways, I thought it might be useful…”
“Your family runs a chocolate farm!?”

…A chocolate farm. What an amazing phrase. Is it a family that makes chocolate? In that case, wouldn’t they be called pastry chefs? No, wait—pastry chefs are confectioners, aren’t they? So, it must be some kind of guild or organization that specializes in making chocolate. I brushed it off at the time, but once I arrived at the village, I concluded there must be trees that bear chocolate.
…Still, those farmers must be at high risk for diabetes.
“I hated working on the chocolate farm, so I ran away from home dreaming of becoming an adventurer… only to end up as a thief.”

Huh… It’s a pretty common storyline—the classic story of someone who had a dream but failed. He mentioned going back home to take over the family business, but what’s it like to take over a chocolate farm? I couldn’t help but think it might actually be kind of fun.
“Lately, I’ve been keeping in touch with my family by letter. I told them, ‘If the Shield Hero wants some chocolate, maybe they’d be willing to buy some?’ I could even act as a go-between.”
“Hmm… I’ll think about it.”
“And… about my dad…”
The Robin Hood-type muttered, then looked away.
“If possible, please negotiate only with my sister and mom. If you take this letter to them, I think they’ll agree! ”
“Ah, uh…”

And that’s how I ended up getting a letter of introduction to a chocolate farm from the Robin Hood. Demand for chocolate is high this season, so prices are on the high side. That said, there’s no real benefit to storing chocolate long-term in my village. I could buy it during the off-season and freeze it with Magic, but that would mean waiting until next year. Apparently, last year’s harvest was poor due to the waves, and prices are on the rise this year.

So… the chocolate farm is located in a colder region, just a short distance from the former territory of Melromarc. If chocolate trees grew in a warm climate, they’d probably just melt, after all… It’s February now, and the fact that they’re harvested during the cold season makes sense, all things considered.
“I’m starting to smell something sweet.”
“Yeah, I do, too.”

As we traveled by carriage, a gradually cloying scent began to waft through the air. It wasn’t just the smell of chocolate—it was simply a sweet smell. It’s a scent I’m not very familiar with. Even in the real world, there probably aren’t many places where you’d smell something like this. Wait a minute. Maybe this is the kind of smell you’d find at a candy factory?
By the way, I’d noticed along the way that quite a lot of chocolate was being sold in the markets due to Valentine’s Day demand. This world really loves its events, doesn’t it?

…Come to think of it, the tradition was originally spread by the Hero, wasn’t it? Has it become a religious observance as well? If every household were required to buy chocolate, well, that would certainly create demand and help the custom take root. Even the accessory merchant’s chain stores were selling chocolate accessories.
What’s the deal with decorating yourself with food? For starters, you shouldn’t be messing around with food… That’s what I think, but I guess that’s just how vibrant the market has become.
“So… where are the farmers who sell chocolate?”
“Hm? Oh, hold on a sec.”
When Raphtalia asked me, I checked the map included with the letter of introduction from the Robin Hood-like figure.
“It’s over there.”
There were tons of chocolate farms… We made our way through a dense grove of chocolate trees. Just seeing this made me feel conflicted. I’d actually seen a real chocolate tree.
The chocolate bars grew in clusters, much like bananas. It was a fantastical sight. Or rather, was it more like a fairy tale? The shape was different from that of a bread tree, too.

The bread trees in my village don’t have those crepe-like, pitcher-plant-style parts. They seem to bear fruit simply from the nutrients they absorb through their roots. At the tip of each bread fruit is a jam-like part that acts like a seed; if you plant it, a new tree sprouts in a matter of days. It’s quite the monster tree, isn’t it?

It could solve our food problem in one fell swoop. The problem is… as Rat’s investigation revealed, it causes significant damage to the soil. If we don’t manage it properly, we could end up with crop rotation problems and barren land in the blink of an eye. We’ve left this area to the Dune and Rumo folks to handle. As a worst-case scenario, we’re securing land to clear and let it rest. Since it’s essentially a bio-plant, as long as we have the seeds, it’ll be fine in a few days.

Anyway, the chocolate tree had chocolate caked all over its trunk. “Why is it stuck on there like this?” I wondered as I approached the trunk—and then I understood. A small, insect-like monster was clinging to the trunk, already dead. This part of the tree is probably similar in structure to the crepe tree.
I wonder if it’s sucking the nutrients out of the insects, too? What a gross tree…
“Lord Naofumi. It looks like there are other kinds of trees besides the chocolate ones?”
I looked in the direction Raphtalia was pointing and noticed trees that looked like candy and others that looked like marshmallows. Is this place Sweets Land or something?!
“A-anyway… let’s head to the chocolate farm.”

The chocolate farmers must be in their busy season too; they were frantically gathering the ripe chocolate and preparing shipments. Farmers had also come to the chocolate tree I’d been watching and were picking the chocolate. So, I decided to ask them while I was there.
“Hey.”
“Yes?”
The chocolate farmer—who didn’t seem to know I was the Shield Hero—turned around with a annoyed expression after being addressed in the middle of his busy work.
“Do you know how to get to this farm?”
“Oh, you mean Rō-boy’s place?”

The farmer, who’d looked like he was annoyed I’d interrupted him while he was busy, now gave me a sympathetic look. What’s up? Is there some kind of problem? If so, I’d have to mete out some justice to those Robin Hood types…

“Well, you’ll have to go straight through town first, then follow the road all the way east. If possible, you should just talk to Rou-bou’s mother and sister. Everyone’s been worried because they’re probably having a hard time over there, too.”
“Huh…”
I wonder… it feels like the kind of place where they’d try to palm me off with some shoddy goods.
“That place… the quality’s actually pretty good, though…”

He must have sensed my thoughts and decided to fill me in. Or rather, is it okay for him to interrupt his work like this? The other merchants are glaring at us, you know? The guys who approach me, looking annoyed, nod as if they understand when the one I spoke to points east. …I’m starting to feel really uneasy.
“Want me to show you the way?”
“No, you’re probably busy, so I don’t want to trouble you that much.”
“Is that so? Well, is there anything else you’re curious about?”
“If you’re hiding something, tell me.”
“Well… you’ll see when you get there. I’d rather not say any more than that… It’s not like we’re ostracizing anyone or anything, though.”
So they’re not hiding anything… but this is really killing my desire to buy.
“Anything else?”
“Once the chocolate is harvested, when will it bear fruit again?”
“At this time of year, it bears fruit quickly—in a month. That’s when the white chocolate will be ready. After that season passes, it’ll be four months.”
White chocolate… so there’s a White Day, too. I’d better be prepared.

Normally it’s a four-month cycle, but does growth speed up as Valentine’s Day approaches? It really is different from the trees back home. Whether it’s the bread tree or the crepe tree, they bear fruit year-round. Is it the difference in the soil…? I wonder what they’re originally made of?
“A Chocolate Monster has appeared!”
Just as we were talking about that, a sludge-like, chocolate-shaped monster appeared.
